designs.title: No.
designs.why: Strong, instantly readable gag: a deadpan cat lying on the word, its paw on the full stop, about to knock it off the table. It reads from 3 m and works in one ink on both white and black. The face drawing is the best part: confident brush line and a perfect unimpressed squint. Up close it falls apart into three hand styles that don't match. The body is clean brush line, the tail is fine mechanical hatching that will plug or moire at print size, and the letters have uneven white dash stripes that look like a clip-art 'wood/tabby' fill, not a drawn mark. The full stop sits politely at the end of the baseline instead of hanging over the edge, so the punchline is implied rather than landed. On the tee it prints small and high, with the lower 45% of the canvas empty.
designs.fix: Unify it into one ink language and land the joke. Make the letters solid, or give them the same brush hatching as the tail, drawn coarser so it holds in print. Then push the full stop half over the end of the ledge under the paw, so the cat is visibly knocking it off.
